passages.text: After the time of Abimelech, a man of Issachar, Tola son of Puah, the son of Dodo, rose up to save Israel. He lived in Shamir, in the hill country of Ephraim.
passages.sermon:
Tola was a man from the tribe of Issachar.
Tola was the son of Puah.
Puah was the son of Dodo.
Tola became a leader after Abimelech died.
Tola rose up to save Israel.
Tola lived in Shamir.
Shamir is in the hill country of Ephraim.
passages.original: וַיָּקָם֩ אַחֲרֵ֨י אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ לְהוֹשִׁ֣יעַ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל תּוֹלָ֧ע בֶּן־ פּוּאָ֛ה בֶּן־ דּוֹד֖וֹ אִ֣ישׁ יִשָּׂשכָ֑ר וְהֽוּא־ יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּשָׁמִ֖יר בְּהַ֥ר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Tola judged Israel twenty-three years, and when he died, he was buried in Shamir.
passages.sermon:
Tola was a man of Issachar.
Tola became a judge over Israel.
He judged Israel for twenty-three years.
Tola died.
People buried Tola in Shamir.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁפֹּט֙ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְשָׁלֹ֖שׁ שָׁנָ֑ה וַיָּ֖מָת וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר בְּשָׁמִֽיר׃פ

passages.text: Tola was followed by Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel twenty-two years.
passages.sermon:
Jair was a man from Gilead.
Jair became the leader after Tola.
Jair judged Israel.
He judged Israel for twenty-two years.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם אַחֲרָ֔יו יָאִ֖יר הַגִּלְעָדִ֑י וַיִּשְׁפֹּט֙ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֖יִם שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys. And they had thirty towns in the land of Gilead, which to this day are called Havvoth-jair.
passages.sermon:
Jair the Gileadite was a judge of Israel.
Jair had thirty sons.
Each son rode on a donkey.
Jair’s sons had thirty towns in the land of Gilead.
People call these towns Havvoth-jair.
They still use this name today.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי־ ל֞וֹ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים בָּנִ֗ים רֹֽכְבִים֙ עַל־ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים עֲיָרִ֔ים וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים עֲיָרִ֖ים לָהֶ֑ם לָהֶ֞ם יִקְרְא֣וּ׀ חַוֺּ֣ת יָאִ֗יר עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַגִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: When Jair died, he was buried in Kamon.
passages.sermon: Jair was a judge of Israel.\r\nJair died.\r\nPeople buried Jair in Kamon.

passages.text: And again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD. They served the Baals, the Ashtoreths, the gods of Aram, Sidon, and Moab, and the gods of the Ammonites and Philistines. Thus they forsook the LORD and did not serve Him.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites did evil.
They did this in the sight of the LORD.
They served the Baals.
They served the Ashtoreths.
They served the gods of Aram.
They served the gods of Sidon.
They served the gods of Moab.
They served the gods of the Ammonites.
They served the gods of the Philistines.
They forsook the LORD.
They did not serve the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֹּסִ֣פוּ׀ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הָרַע֮ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָה֒ וַיַּעַבְד֣וּ אֶת־ הַבְּעָלִ֣ים וְאֶת־ הָעַשְׁתָּר֡וֹת וְאֶת־ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲרָם֩ וְאֶת־ אֱלֹהֵ֨י צִיד֜וֹן וְאֵ֣ת׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י מוֹאָ֗ב וְאֵת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י בְנֵי־ עַמּ֔וֹן וְאֵ֖ת אֱלֹהֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּעַזְב֥וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א עֲבָדֽוּהוּ׃

passages.text: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hands of the Philistines and Ammonites, who that very year harassed and oppressed the Israelites, and did so for eighteen years to all the Israelites on the other side of the Jordan in Gilead, the land of the Amorites.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD became very angry with Israel.
The LORD gave Israel into the power of the Philistines.
The LORD also gave Israel into the power of the Ammonites.
That year, the Philistines and Ammonites hurt the Israelites.
They crushed and oppressed the Israelites.
They did this for eighteen years.
They hurt all the Israelites who lived east of the Jordan River.
These Israelites lived in Gilead.
Gilead is the land of the Amorites.
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּמְכְּרֵם֙ בְּיַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּבְיַ֖ד בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃ וַֽיִּרְעֲצ֤וּ וַיְרֹֽצְצוּ֙ אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִ֑יא שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֜ה שָׁנָ֗ה אֶֽת־ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּגִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, and Israel was in deep distress.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites were enemies of Israel.
The Ammonites crossed the Jordan River.
They came to fight against Judah.
They also fought against Benjamin.
They also fought against the house of Ephraim.
Israel became very distressed.
passages.original: וַיַּעַבְר֤וּ בְנֵֽי־ עַמּוֹן֙ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לְהִלָּחֵ֛ם גַּם־ בִּיהוּדָ֥ה וּבְבִנְיָמִ֖ין וּבְבֵ֣ית אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַתֵּ֥צֶר לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, saying, “We have sinned against You, for we have indeed forsaken our God and served the Baals.”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites spoke to the LORD.
They cried out to Him.
They said, “We have sinned against You.”
They said, “We left our God.”
They said, “We served the Baals.”
passages.original: וַֽיִּזְעֲקוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־ יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר חָטָ֣אנוּ לָ֔ךְ וְכִ֤י עָזַ֙בְנוּ֙ אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ וַֽנַּעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־ הַבְּעָלִֽים׃פ

passages.text: The LORD replied, “When the Egyptians, Amorites, Ammonites, Philistines, Sidonians, Amalekites, and Maonites oppressed you and you cried out to Me, did I not save you from their hands?
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to the Israelites.
He reminded them of their history.
He said, “The Egyptians oppressed you.
The Amorites oppressed you.
The Ammonites oppressed you.
The Philistines oppressed you.
The Sidonians oppressed you.
The Amalekites oppressed you.
The Maonites oppressed you.
You cried out to Me for help.
I saved you from their hands.”
passages.original: וַ֥יֹּאמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הֲלֹ֤א מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ וּמִן־ הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י וּמִן־ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן וּמִן־ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃ וְצִידוֹנִ֤ים וַֽעֲמָלֵק֙ וּמָע֔וֹן לָחֲצ֖וּ אֶתְכֶ֑ם וַתִּצְעֲק֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וָאוֹשִׁ֥יעָה אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדָֽם׃

passages.text: But you have forsaken Me and served other gods, so I will no longer save you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to the Israelites.
The LORD said, “You have abandoned Me.
You have served other gods.
Therefore, I will not save you again.”
passages.original: וְאַתֶּם֙ עֲזַבְתֶּ֣ם אוֹתִ֔י וַתַּעַבְד֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים לָכֵ֥ן לֹֽא־ אוֹסִ֖יף לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them save you in your time of trouble.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to the Israelites.
He said, "Go to the gods you have chosen.
Cry out to them.
Let those gods save you when you are in trouble."
passages.original: לְכ֗וּ וְזַֽעֲקוּ֙ אֶל־ הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּחַרְתֶּ֖ם בָּ֑ם הֵ֛מָּה יוֹשִׁ֥יעוּ לָכֶ֖ם בְּעֵ֥ת צָרַתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: “We have sinned,” the Israelites said to the LORD. “Deal with us as You see fit; but please deliver us today!”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites spoke to the LORD.
They said, “We have sinned.”
They said, “Do to us whatever seems good to You.”
They said, “But please save us today.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶל־ יְהוָה֙ חָטָ֔אנוּ עֲשֵׂה־ אַתָּ֣ה לָ֔נוּ כְּכָל־ הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ אַ֛ךְ הַצִּילֵ֥נוּ נָ֖א הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD, and He could no longer bear the misery of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites removed the foreign gods from among them.
They served the LORD.
The LORD saw the suffering of Israel.
He could no longer bear their misery.
passages.original: וַיָּסִ֜ירוּ אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַנֵּכָר֙ מִקִּרְבָּ֔ם וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֑ה וַתִּקְצַ֥ר נַפְשׁ֖וֹ בַּעֲמַ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: Then the Ammonites were called to arms and camped in Gilead, and the Israelites assembled and camped at Mizpah.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites gathered their army.
They camped in Gilead.
The Israelites also assembled their people.
They camped at Mizpah.
passages.original: וַיִּצָּֽעֲקוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּגִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֵּאָֽסְפוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּמִּצְפָּֽה׃

passages.text: And the rulers of Gilead said to one another, “Whoever will launch the attack against the Ammonites will be the head of all who live in Gilead.”
passages.sermon:
The rulers of Gilead spoke to each other.
They were the leaders of the people in Gilead.
They asked a question.
They said, “Who will begin the fight against the Ammonites?”
They made a promise.
They said, “That man will become the leader of everyone who lives in Gilead.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ הָעָ֜ם שָׂרֵ֤י גִלְעָד֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֔הוּ מִ֣י הָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָחֵ֔ל לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בִּבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לְרֹ֔אשׁ לְכֹ֖ל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י גִלְעָֽד׃פ
